# tooling/install — one-command editor setup
<!-- generated by cx-tooling-author; edits will be overwritten on next render -->

One command per editor, or one for everything:

```sh
tooling/install/install.sh            # preflight + LSP check + Neovim + VS Code
tooling/install/install-nvim.sh       # Neovim >= 0.11 only
tooling/install/install-vscode.sh     # VS Code only
tooling/install/uninstall.sh          # remove what install.sh placed
```

What `install-nvim.sh` does:
1. builds + installs the tree-sitter grammar via `make -C tooling/tree-sitter-cx
   install-nvim` — the parser is ad-hoc **signed**, installed to a **fresh
   inode**, and the target ends with a headless **load-proof** (a bad parser
   fails the install instead of killing your editor; #883);
2. writes a lazy.nvim spec at `~/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/cx.lua` with a
   `dir =` entry pointing at this checkout's plugin root
   (`tooling/neovim` — native `vim.lsp.config`, no nvim-lspconfig), backing up
   any hand-edited spec first; plain-Neovim installs copy the plugin root into
   `site/pack/cx/start/` instead;
3. smoke-tests the plugin headless before declaring success.

What `install-vscode.sh` does: picks (or builds) the newest
`tooling/vscode/cx-language-*.vsix` and installs it with `code
--install-extension`.

The LSP is the `cx` binary itself (`cx lsp`, JSON-RPC over stdio) — point
`CX_BIN` (Neovim) or `cx.serverPath` (VS Code) at a checkout build, or put
`cx` on `PATH`. `preflight.sh` reports missing prerequisites before anything
is written; every script is idempotent and backs up hand-edited files.
